description:

lines.text: Good evening, neighbors. Welcome to the slowest, scariest walk on the block.
The rules are simple. Walk toward the porch. Very slowly. Very menacingly. Then reveal.
I've been practicing my menacing face since August.
I've been practicing since breakfast. Which was also my second breakfast.
I didn't know there was a competition. I came out to get the mail.
Too late, Marcus. You're contestant number one. Begin your walk.
Okay. Walking. Slowly.
Oh, he's good. He's really slow.
That's just how he walks. I've seen him walk to the fridge.
Still walking. My knee is making a noise.
The knee noise is very spooky. Points for atmosphere.
And here is my reveal.
And what are you dressed as, Marcus?
A dad who forgot it was Halloween.
That's the scariest thing I've ever heard.
It gets worse. I also forgot to buy candy.
No!
Marcus, that is a horror story. Nine out of ten.
No. Contestant number two. Pickles, take us away.
Rule one. Nobody say the word walk in a happy voice. I'll lose focus.
Walk!
Where? Are we going? Is it a walk? Oh, I'm so happy.
Junie, please don't sabotage the contestants.
Okay. I'm back. I'm menacing. Here I come.
And here is my reveal.
Little red horns. Very bold. Are you a devil?
No. I'm dressed as the mailman.
The mailman doesn't have horns.
To me he does. He comes every day. He touches our door. Nobody stops him.
He brings us the mail, buddy.
That's what he wants you to think.
Deeply personal. Slightly unhinged. Eight and a half.
Final contestant. Junie, show us your walk.
Close your eyes and listen to me roll menacingly.
She's rolling. She's rolling the wrong way.
The driveway is a hill. I'm a pumpkin. Physics is not my friend.
Okay. I'm back. And here is my reveal.
Junie. What are you dressed as?
A pumpkin.
You are a pumpkin.
Exactly. I committed. Some people call it lazy. I call it method.
Next year I'm going as something truly scary.
What's scarier than a pumpkin?
A pie. In late November. Don't ask me how I know.
Chilling. Ten out of ten for the pie.
Hang on. Delphine, you haven't done your walk.
Very well. But I don't really walk.
Wait. She's floating. Where are your feet?
I haven't had feet since nineteen fifty two.
So that's not a bedsheet?
No, darling. I live in your porch light. I've judged this walk for seventy years.
Ahh!
Is it scary being a real ghost?
Not at all. The scariest thing I've seen all night is a man with no candy.
I said I was sorry.
The winner is me. Same time next year. Marcus, bring candy.
Sure. What day is Halloween again?
